state_code: # STATUS: FINAL. 2026 South Dakota Mathematics Standards (replace the 2018 CCSS-based set).
# - Adopted by the South Dakota Board of Education Standards on May 4, 2026 (document cover: "Adopted May 4, 2026").
# - SD DOE "Assessed Standards Timeline": Math adopted 2026, transition 2026-2027, implement 2027-2028, state assessment 2028-2029.
# - News at adoption (KOTA, May 5 2026) says the board approved them knowing minor non-content corrections may follow; no corrected
#   edition was posted as of 2026-10-01. Recheck the PDF before relying on exact wording.
# - South Dakota Mathematics Standards, adopted May 4, 2026 (K-5 on document pp. 1-15):
# - SD DOE math standards page (lists "Mathematics Standards 2026" and "2018"): https://doe.sd.gov/contentstandards/math.aspx
# - No official 2026-to-CCSS or 2018-to-2026 crosswalk was found. Every mapping here is my own reading of the 2026 text against CCSS.
# - Grade.Domain.Number, e.g. K.N.1, 3.M.17, 4.MF.2. Numbers run on through a grade's domain; no cluster letter in the code.
#   Clusters are named headings only (e.g. "Names, Sequence, & Counting", "Place Value", "Time and Money", "Data", "Shapes").
# - No lettered sub-parts. Standards for Mathematical Practice (8) are printed up front and skipped here.
# - N Numbers; OA Operations and Algebraic Thinking; M Measurement (includes time, money, data); G Geometry (includes angles,
#   volume and the coordinate plane in grades 4-5); MF Mathematical Fluency; F Fractions (grade 2 "Fraction Foundation", grades 3-5).
# - Grade 2's only F standard (2.F.1) and grade 1's partitioning (1.G.5) are CCSS geometry content.
# - Fully: 2.MD.A.2 (measure one object with two units), 2.MD.A.4 (how much longer), 2.MD.B.5 (length word problems),
#   2.MD.B.6 (whole numbers as lengths on a number line; only "open number lines" as a strategy in 2.OA.2).
# - Partly: composing 3D shapes (1.G.A.2); 2.MD.D.9 line plots of measured lengths (line plots are generic in 2.M.12);
#   "interpret expressions without evaluating" (5.OA.A.2); fraction operations on line-plot data (5.MD.B.2);
#   3.OA.C.7 division fluency and products from memory move to grade 4 (4.MF.1-2); grade 3 memory is facts for 0,1,2,5,10 only (3.MF.2);
#   no explicit making-ten or other named strategies (1.OA.C.6); 3D shape comparison in K (K.G.B.4).
# - New: K.M.3 (clock and time of day), K.M.4 (calendar), 2.N.5 (distance to next/previous ten or hundred), 2.G.3 (regular vs irregular shapes),
# - Moved earlier: money from K (pennies, dimes) and grade 1 (all coins, mixed coins to $1) - CCSS has money only in 2.MD.C.8;
#   grade 1 subtracts a one-digit from a two-digit number (CCSS 2.NBT.B.5); grade 2 elapsed time (3.MD.A.1), quadrilateral types (3.G.A.1);
#   grade 3 four-digit place value and numbers to 10,000 (4.NBT.A.2), money with decimals (2.MD.C.8 + 4.NF.C.6), polygons by sides (2.G.A.1);
#   grade 4 order of operations without parentheses (3.OA.D.8 note / 5.OA.A.1).
# - Moved later: all multiplication and division facts from memory in grade 4 (CCSS 3.OA.C.7).
# - Higher bars: fluency within 20 in grade 1 (CCSS 2.OA.B.2), subtraction facts to 20 from memory in grade 2, fluent multi-digit division in grade 5
#   (CCSS 6.NS.B.2; not a K-5 code, so 5.MF.2 is mapped to 5.NBT.B.6 as edited).
# - Also: counting backward (K-2), skip-counting by 2s and 5s, odd/even to 50, bills to $100 in grade 2, customary units for liquid volume and mass
#   in grade 3, circle and line graphs in grade 3, straight angles, trapezoid as exactly one pair of parallel sides (4.G.7),
# - kind: "same" = CCSS content at the same grade with nothing added, including a standard that covers only part of one CCSS standard
#   (SD often splits one CCSS standard into several, e.g. 3.M.1-3.M.8, 5.G.11-5.G.14). "edited" = same grade but content added, limits changed,
#   or a grade-level shift in expectation. "moved" = main content is CCSS from another grade (that code in ccss). "new" = no CCSS counterpart.
# - Money rows (K.M.5, K.M.6, 1.M.4, 1.M.5) marked moved from 2.MD.C.8; could be read as new.
# - Properties standards 2.OA.1 and 4.OA.12 mapped to 2.NBT.B.5 / 4.NBT.B.5 (CCSS uses properties inside those strategy standards).
# - K.MF.3 (recognizing small amounts at a glance, i.e. subitizing) mapped to K.CC.B.5 as edited; could be new.
# - 1.MF.1-2 list 2.OA.B.2 because fluency within 20 is CCSS grade 2; 2.M.8 (time problems in 5-minute steps) mapped to 3.MD.A.1.
# - 3.MF.2 wording ("multiplication facts (0-12) to include 0, 1, 2, 5, and 10") is ambiguous; read as facts with those factors.
# - Text was extracted from the PDF; inequality symbols and some italic variables (n, x, y, a/b) are displaced in extraction, which does not change codes.
